newsitem.title: CONGO: Kabila boards ship for Zaire talks.
newsitem.headline: Kabila boards ship for Zaire talks.

text.p: Rebel leader Laurent Kabila boarded a South African ship in Congo on Saturday for talks with veteran president Mobutu Sese Seko, a South African spokesman said.
Foreign Ministry spokesman Pieter Swanepoel told reporters on board the SAS Outeniqua, moored in Congo's port of Pointe Noire, that Kabila arrived by helicopter. Mobutu had yet to board.
"We are now entering into a third day," Swanepoel told the reporters earlier, before Kabila arrived.
Mandela and Mobutu boarded the ship on Friday and sailed into international waters for a rendezvous with Kabila, who failed to show, citing security concerns.
Mobutu left the ship late on Friday and spent the night and Saturday in Pointe Noire.
Mandela remained on board while diplomatic efforts continued to persuade the two civil war rivals to join him there.

"I have told (South African) President Nelson Mandela that Mobutu would have to resign immediately our talks start otherwise my forces are under instructions to move into Kinshasa should he refuse," Kabila added. He expected his forces to be 80 km (50 miles) from Kinshasa by Sunday evening.
Minutes after Kabila spoke, Mobutu boarded the ship, which has been waiting off the Congolese port of Pointe Noire since Friday as Mandela tried to arrange the peace talks.
Kabila said he had protested to Mandela about security on the ship and the fact the rebels had been excluded from the arrangements for the talks.

"I have strongly protested to President Mandela because the security arrangements on the ship are appalling to say the least. The South Africaans had allowed over 100 Zairean security men to board the ship and they also cheated me by flying me to the Congolese port when I had objected," he said.
